faq: Which help desks do you work with?
Zendesk, Freshdesk, Help Scout, Gorgias, Intercom, Zoho Desk and shared Gmail or Outlook inboxes. If yours has an official connection or API, we can usually link it.
Do you need admin access to my help desk?
Usually an admin or agent seat with enough rights to add the connection. You invite us from your own account and can remove access when we finish.
Will my current tickets be changed?
No. We connect new traffic and test on copies or a small batch first. Existing tickets are untouched unless you ask us to tidy tags.
Can you move me to a different help desk?
A full move with old tickets is a bigger job than this package. Ask for a quote and we scope it separately after reviewing your volume.
desc:
Connecting your help desk, email and chat tools puts every customer conversation in one place. Ecom Swift LLC links the systems you already use, so tickets are created automatically and each agent sees the customer, the order and the history without switching tabs.

## What does it mean to connect help desk, email and chat tools?

Connecting these tools means that a message arriving in one place, such as a live chat window or a shared inbox, creates or updates a ticket in your help desk. Customer details travel with it. The agent opens a single screen and sees who is writing, what they bought and what was said before.

## The cost of support scattered across tools

When chat lives in one app, email in another and tickets in a third, agents copy and paste between them. Context gets lost. A customer who chatted yesterday and emails today looks like a stranger, and two agents may answer the same message twice.

Scattered tools also make problems invisible. Nobody can say how many conversations are open, which ones are overdue or which customers wrote three times. Connections turn a set of separate inboxes into one queue that a team can actually manage.

## How linked tools change daily work

A connected setup saves the small, constant effort of re-typing names, searching for order numbers and forwarding messages. That time goes back into answering. Customers notice the difference because agents greet them by name and already know the order.

It also reduces mistakes. Duplicate tickets get merged, internal alerts tell the right person when something new arrives, and tags and macros keep wording consistent. When something stops working, a failure alert reaches your team instead of a customer complaint.

## What a well-connected support setup includes

- New chats and emails creating tickets without manual entry.
- Customer name and email passed to the ticket automatically.
- Order details from your store shown inside the ticket.
- Rules that merge duplicate tickets from the same customer and topic.
- An internal alert when a new ticket arrives or a ticket stays unanswered.
- Tags that group tickets by topic or status.
- Macros, which are saved replies agents insert in one click.
- Customer history visible on every ticket.
- Alerts to your team if a connection breaks.
- A written map showing where every message goes.

## How we work

We start by listing the tools you use and drawing how a message should travel between them. We then connect each tool using limited access in your own accounts, so you stay the owner of every system. Each link is tested with real messages before we call it finished, and we record the setup in a simple connection map.

The Basic package links two tools and creates tickets automatically. The Standard package connects up to three tools, shows store details in tickets and adds merging rules and alerts. The Premium package connects more tools, sets up tags and macros, adds failure alerts and ends with a recorded handover video. We do not change your existing tickets unless you ask.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which tool is the single home for tickets.
- Keep a short list of who owns each connection.
- Test with a real message after any change to the tools.
- Use clear tag names that agents understand at a glance.

**Avoid:**
- Connecting tools you no longer use.
- Giving a connection wider access than it needs.
- Creating tags for every possible case on day one.
- Running two systems that both create tickets for the same message.
- Skipping the failure alerts.

## Who this is for

A store owner whose chat, Gmail and help desk do not talk to each other. A support lead who wants order details inside every ticket. A team switching from a shared inbox to a proper help desk who wants the pieces linked before the move.

## What we need from you

A list of the tools you use and the login role we should join as, such as admin, staff or collaborator. We never need your password. Tell us what a good ticket looks like for your team, and we will build the connections around it.
